title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 58 (Alternative promise, one branch being illegal)

content.overview: Section 58 provides that in the case of an alternative promise, one branch of which is legal and the other illegal, the legal branch alone can be enforced.
content.glance: Alternative promise with one legal and one illegal branch → only the legal branch enforceable.
content.study: Where an alternative promise has one legal branch and one illegal branch, only the legal branch can be enforced. Current-law framing: identify the alternative branches; enforce the legal branch only; treat the illegal branch as unenforceable.

sections.heading: Legal branch alone
sections.body: In an alternative promise with one legal and one illegal branch, the legal branch alone can be enforced.

provisions.title: Alternative promise, one branch being illegal

examples.title: Alternative legal or illegal act
examples.body: A promises to pay B ₹1,000 or to deliver stolen goods. Only the payment branch can be enforced under s. 58.

hypotheticals.question: Can the illegal alternative still be chosen by the promisor?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 58: only the legal branch can be enforced; the illegal branch cannot.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-58
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: The whole alternative promise is void if one branch is illegal.
misconceptions.correction: Section 58 allows enforcement of the legal branch alone.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 58 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify alternative branches. II. Enforce legal branch only. III. Conclude illegal branch unenforceable.

examTips: State that only the legal branch is enforceable.
